hook: I painted my oak cabinets for $89, not $12,000

scenes.visual_prompt: Close-up of a handwritten contractor estimate reading $5,000-$20,000 next to dated glossy orange oak cabinets
scenes.voiceover: Every quote I got for these cabinets started at five figures.

scenes.visual_prompt: Hand running along dated glossy orange-toned oak cabinet door, camera close on wood grain
scenes.on_screen_text: The wood's fine. The color isn't.
scenes.voiceover: The wood underneath is structurally fine — it's just orange and shiny.

scenes.visual_prompt: Unboxing an $89 cabinet paint kit on a kitchen counter, box label visible
scenes.voiceover: This $89 kit is behind most of the 'paint your cabinets' posts right now.

scenes.visual_prompt: Wiping cabinet door with deglosser cloth, grease residue visible before the wipe
scenes.voiceover: First pass is deglosser — it won't grip over kitchen grime.

scenes.visual_prompt: Paint counter employee tinting a can of bonding coat to match a burnt-orange chip
scenes.voiceover: It doesn't ship burnt-orange — you bring the bonding coat in and get it tinted.

scenes.visual_prompt: Reveal shot of finished burnt-orange cabinets with new black hardware in a full kitchen
scenes.voiceover: A full kitchen runs two kits, so closer to $160 to $180 total.

scenes.visual_prompt: Text card showing math: $180 versus $20,000 replacement quote crossed out
scenes.voiceover: Still under 2 percent of what replacement quoted me.

caption: I got quoted $5,000-$20,000 to replace my oak cabinets. Instead I spent $89 on a kit, plus $91 more for a second one, and ended up with the burnt-orange HGTV and BHG are both pushing this week. Full breakdown — tinting, cure time, what actually went wrong — on the blog.
